_: WHAT A BUILD COSTS, WRITTEN DOWN SO CI CAN CHECK IT.
These are the runtime fingerprints of the app as it stands. An EAS Update
only ever reaches a build whose fingerprint matches it, so while these two
numbers hold still, every change ships to an installed phone for free. The
moment one moves, every copy already on a handset is cut off until somebody
spends a build — and on iOS that is a handful a month.
WHY IT IS A FILE AND NOT A HABIT. It used to be a habit. Commits through
7.332.0, 7.335.0 and 7.338.0 each recorded 'the fingerprint is e44c3556…
before and after' — somebody computing it by hand every time and writing it
down. After 7.327.0 that stopped, and three native changes went through
unnoticed: two Expo packages at 7.328.0, the camera at 7.329.0, and the
opaque iOS icon at 7.349.0. Nobody found out until a phone sat on an old
version taking no updates and the reason took an hour to work out.
A pull request that moves either number now fails, and says what it costs.
If the change is wanted, `npm run fingerprint` rewrites this file and the
diff records which change spent the build.
